subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle for Telegram and WhatsApp

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this core-owned durable ingress lifecycle as a permanent public Plugin SDK contract now, and if so how narrow should that contract be?
rationale: The branch moves ownership from bundled channel code into core and adds a large permanent SDK surface; correctness repairs are mechanical, but the core/plugin boundary and public compatibility obligation require maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve a narrow core seam
options.body: Keep the core drain and channel migrations, but export only the high-level drain and lifecycle contract after the four blockers and live proof are complete.

options.title: Keep the broad SDK surface
options.body: Accept the low-level owner, claim, and retry exports as supported plugin contracts and require comprehensive compatibility documentation and tests.

options.title: Pause and split the work
options.body: Land an internal core drain first and defer public SDK exposure or one channel migration to a separately reviewed change.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core seam
recommendation.body: Keep the core drain and channel migrations, but export only the high-level drain and lifecycle contract after the four blockers and live proof are complete.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged SDK contract-narrowing work makes them the strongest available owner for deciding the acceptable permanent public surface.
